coverage: John Washam's self-study CS curriculum in one long README (CC BY-SA 4.0): study method, language choice, books, then a checkbox list of topics: Big-O, data structures, trees, sorting, graphs, recursion/DP, design patterns, OS and networking, plus optional system design and advanced topics. Each section is mostly links to university lectures and articles, sometimes with an implement-it checklist. No problems or own explanations. All free; many links are 2009-2016 era.

refs.title: Data Structures: Arrays
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Lecture videos on static and dynamic arrays, then a build-it-yourself checklist for a resizable vector with amortised-cost notes. Good fundamentals drill; no interview problems.

refs.title: Data Structures: Hash table
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Chaining and open-addressing lectures (MIT), PyCon talks on dict internals, and an implement-with-linear-probing checklist. Theory-first, not pattern-oriented.

refs.title: Data Structures: Linked Lists
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Intro videos plus a long implement-every-operation checklist (push/pop front/back, insert, reverse, remove value). Solid way to build linked-list fluency before pattern problems.

refs.title: Data Structures: Stack
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: One short review video and a note that a stack is trivial to build on an array; thin section. The Queue section next to it is similar.

refs.title: Binary search
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: A few videos, a TopCoder article and a link to a reusable binary-search template, plus implement iterative and recursive search. No rotated-array or search-on-answer practice.

refs.title: Bitwise operations
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Reading list on bit operators and bit hacks, two's complement, counting set bits, swap and absolute-value tricks; links the repo's bits cheat sheet.

refs.title: Bits cheat sheet (PDF)
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Repo-hosted one-page table of powers of two with max/min signed and unsigned int values per bit width. Narrow: a number-range reference, not bit tricks.

refs.title: Trees intro and traversals
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Tree basics, BFS/DFS and pre/in/post-order traversal videos with notes on time and space per traversal. Concept only, no problem practice.

refs.title: Heap / Priority Queue / Binary Heap
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Heap lectures plus a checklist to implement a max-heap with sift up/down, heapify and heap sort.

refs.title: Sorting
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Long section: stability, which sorts suit lists vs arrays, Sedgewick/Berkeley lectures, implement merge sort and quicksort, optional radix/counting sort. One of the denser sections.

refs.title: Graphs
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Graph representations, BFS/DFS, Dijkstra, MST, SCC lectures, and an implement list incl. cycle check, topological sort, connected components, bipartite check.

refs.title: Recursion (and backtracking blueprint)
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Stanford recursion/backtracking lectures, tail recursion, and links to a general backtracking template discussion for subsets/permutations/combination sum.

refs.title: Dynamic Programming
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Skiena and Simonson DP lectures plus Coursera clips; no pattern breakdown. Its claim that DP rarely appears in interviews is dated.

refs.title: Combinatorics & Probability
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Short list of factorial/permutation/combination and probability videos (Khan Academy).

refs.title: String searching & manipulations
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Substring search lectures: brute force, KMP, Boyer-Moore, Rabin-Karp, suffix arrays.

refs.title: Tries
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Trie lectures (R-way, ternary) and articles; read-only, author says don't implement. We have no tries topic.

refs.title: Processes and Threads
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: OS concurrency checklist: processes vs threads, locks, mutexes, semaphores, monitors, deadlock, context switching, plus C++ and Python concurrency talks. Background, not interview problems.

refs.title: Caches (LRU)
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Three videos on LRU cache design incl. a LeetCode 146 walkthrough, plus CPU cache lectures.

refs.title: Big-O cheat sheet (PDF)
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Repo copy of the bigocheatsheet.com chart: operation costs for common data structures and best/average/worst for array sorting algorithms. Quick pre-interview review.

refs.title: Design patterns
refs.subject: ood
refs.summary: Checklist of 17 patterns to learn, mostly GoF (strategy, adapter, observer, etc.), a UML review video, a video series and a Head First recommendation. List only, no worked designs.

refs.title: System Design, Scalability, Data Handling
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Optional section: a 3-step interview flow (scope, estimate, abstract design), long reading list of mostly 2009-2016 posts (CAP, consistent hashing, sharding, Raft) and 6 practice prompts. Starts you at the System Design Primer.

refs.title: System design cheat sheet (PDF)
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: One-page PDF of the same 3-step design flow as the README (scope and use cases, estimate load and storage, layered abstract design). Useful printable checklist.

refs.title: Networking
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Videos on TCP vs UDP, OSI model, HTTP, HTTP/2, TLS, sockets and CIDR.

refs.title: Messaging, Serialization, and Queueing Systems
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Link list of tools: Thrift, Protocol Buffers, gRPC, Redis, SQS/SNS, RabbitMQ, Celery, ZeroMQ, Kafka, Avro. Product homepages, no comparison.

refs.title: Computer Security
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: MIT security lecture playlist (threat models, web security, network security). Broad security, not auth design.
